THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Tandoori Chicken Drumsticks

One marinade base, two spice levels. Adults get the full Shan (or Everest) tandoori masala — 3 drumsticks, 525 cal, 60g protein. Kids get the same yogurt-and-lemon base with roughly a sixth of the spice, plus a carb they recognize. Both batches hit the same rack at the same time. Overnight marinade is non-negotiable.

YIELD4 servings
TOTAL TIME30 min + overnight marinade
COOK METHODOven · Grill
EST. / SERVING~525 cal | ~60g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: Cut 2-3 deep slits per drumstick TO THE BONE — don't half-ass this.

Ingredients

BASE

  • 8-10 skinless chicken drumsticks
  • 1 container fat-free Greek yogurt (~150-170g)
  • Juice of 1 lemon

SIDES

  • Cucumber + kala namak (black salt)
  • Onion + Kashmiri chili + lemon

SHARED SIDE

  • Cucumber

ADULT MARINADE

  • 2/3 packet Shan or Everest Tandoori Masala
  • Pinch red color (optional)

Option 1

  • About 1/6 packet tandoori masala (stirred into the reserved yogurt-lemon base)
  • Cucumber slices
  • ~200 cal of a familiar Indian carb — rice, naan, or bhatura

Allergens: dairy. Kid carb is optional — naan and bhatura contain wheat; rice keeps the plate gluten free

SPLIT HAPPENS AT MARINATION — not at cooking. Mix the yogurt + lemon base, pull the kid portion out, then spice the adult bowl to full strength. Both bowls rest overnight; both batches hit the same rack at the same time.

Method

Shared base

  1. 1.PREP. Pull the skin off, pat the drumsticks dry, cut 2-3 deep slits per piece — to the bone. Split into an adult pile (5-6) and a kid pile (3-4).
  2. 2.BASE. Mix the fat-free Greek yogurt with the lemon juice. Pull out about a third for the kid bowl BEFORE any masala goes in.
  3. 3.MARINATE ADULT. Load 2/3 packet of tandoori masala into the remaining yogurt base. Massage deep into the slits until every piece is thickly coated.
  4. 4.MARINATE KID. Stir about one-sixth of the packet into the reserved base. Same flavor, quiet enough for a 5-year-old. Massage in.
  5. 5.REST. Both bowls covered, overnight in the fridge. Minimum 6 hours.
  6. 6.COOK. Space the drumsticks on a wire rack over a sheet pan — no touching. Bake 425°F 15-20 min, then broil 5-7 min per side. OR grill medium-high 10-15 min per side. Pull at 165°F internal with visible char.

Adult — Full Tandoori, 3 Drumsticks

  1. 7.SPICY ONIONS. Toss thin-sliced red onion with Kashmiri chili and a hard squeeze of lemon. Let it sit while the chicken rests — it slumps and turns bright red.
  2. 8.PLATE. 3 drumsticks per adult on a white plate. Tip the spicy onions on alongside, add sliced cucumber sprinkled with kala namak. 525 cal / 60g protein.

Kid — Mild Tandoori + Carb · Option 1

  1. 7.PLATE. 1 drumstick in the big compartment, cucumber in the round well, the carb in the third. Nothing touching — kids control the assembly.
  2. 8.Adjust the portion to your kid's appetite. 1 drumstick + ~200 cal carb lands around 385 cal / 25g protein.

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult — Full Tandoori, 3 Drumsticks: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid — Mild Tandoori + Carb: Serve the kid portion as described above.

Keys to success

  • Overnight marinade minimum. 6 hours if you're in a rush.
  • Don't add salt — Shan and Everest masalas already have it. Extra salt = inedible.

If something fails

Outside burnt, inside raw: You broiled from the start. Bake first at 425°F for 15-20 min, flip halfway, THEN broil to char.

No flavor / bland: Slits weren't deep enough, or you didn't marinate overnight. Both are non-negotiable.

Chicken is dry: Overcooked. Internal temp 165°F, pull immediately. The yogurt should keep it moist if you don't overcook.

Too spicy for adults: Use 1/2 packet of masala instead of 2/3. The heat is front-loaded — it mellows with yogurt.

Kids won't eat it: Cut the masala further — a tenth of the packet instead of a sixth. The point is that they're eating the same thing you are, just quieter. If they're still resistant, the carb does the work: bhatura, naan, or rice on the tray makes the plate familiar.

Kid drumstick came out as spicy as the adult one: You marinated them in the same bowl, or you loaded the masala into the shared yogurt base before pulling the kid portion. Mix the yogurt + lemon first, remove the kid share, THEN spice the adult bowl.

Storage and reheating

Store: Marinated drumsticks keep 2 days in the fridge before cooking. Cooked drumsticks keep 4 days. Store cucumber, onions, and the carb separately.

Reheat: Air fryer 375°F for 5 min to re-crisp, or oven until the center hits 165°F. Microwave works if you don't care about the char.

Lasts: Cooked: 4 days in fridge. Marinated raw: 2 days.

Estimated nutrition

~525 cal | ~60g protein.

525 cal / 60g protein is the 3-drumstick adult plate with cucumber and spicy onions — the site previously listed the 2-drumstick version at 350 cal / 40g. Same recipe, bigger plate. Scale down by a third if you're eating two.

Make this when

You want tandoori that actually tastes like tandoori — deep spice from a full-strength masala, yogurt tenderized, visible char from the grill or broiler. One marinade base, two spice levels: full power for adults, about a sixth of the masala for kids.

Watch the full cook

Brands I use

Shan
Tandoori Masala
Real Pakistani spice blend — not the watered-down grocery store version. This is what makes it taste like tandoori. Everest's tandoori masala is the equivalent Indian blend and behaves the same way.
Fage
Total 0% Greek Yogurt
Thick, high protein, tenderizes the chicken — the marinade base for both the adult and kid bowls
